S39.02.needs: a saved memory first (see S39.10) to check the effect
S39.02.note: The Memory screen is also reached from Profile > Local settings > Memory in Local mode. The exact place of the Open menu button on the chat tab was not confirmed in code.
steps: From the chat screen, tap Open menu, then tap Settings.
Under Assistant, tap Memory.
Look under MEMORY CONTROLS for the switch labelled Memory and turn it off.
Read the line Memory is off, so new memories can't be added or imported. and the Turn on button that appears.
Start a new chat and ask about a fact you saved earlier; the assistant should not use it while Memory is off.
Turn Memory back on and check the saved facts are used again.
S39.02.where: Open menu > Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch labelled Memory at the top

S39.03.needs: one older chat with a distinct topic
S39.03.note: Code default is on for Local and off for Cloud (localSettingsStore and cloudSettingsStore).
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Turn off the switch labelled Search and reference chats.
Start a new chat and ask about something that was only in an older chat.
Check the assistant does not bring in excerpts from other past chats.
Turn the switch on and ask the same question again to compare.
S39.03.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch labelled Search and reference chats

S39.04.needs: a few saved memories (add them with S39.10 first); with none, the screen shows No memories yet
S39.04.note: Local mode also opens this screen from Profile > Local settings > Memory.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Scroll down past the switches and the rows Memory summary and Replaced memories.
Read the count line under those rows, for example a number.
Scroll the list and check each saved memory appears as a card.
S39.04.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory (the list below the controls)

S39.05.needs: two or more saved memories with different words
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the field with the placeholder Search memories....
Type one word that appears in a saved memory.
Check the list shows only matching memories.
Tap the clear control on the field, then tap the chip Pinned to filter to pinned memories.
S39.05.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the field Search memories...

S39.06.needs: saved memories of several kinds (for example facts, preferences and decisions learned from chats)
S39.06.note: Headings appear only when there are at least two topic groups. The code has no work or background topic: the groups are Preferences, About you, Decisions, Context, Summaries and Skills.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Make sure the chip All is selected and the search field is empty.
Look for section headings between the memory cards.
Compare the headings with the Expected topics.
S39.06.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, with the chip All selected and the search field empty

S39.09.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with some Cloud chats
S39.09.note: The Work in progress section appears only when the recap has ongoing work.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and switch to Cloud mode.
Open Settings and find the section Cloud.
Tap Reflect.
Look for the heading Work in progress and read the ongoing projects listed under it.
S39.09.where: Settings > Cloud > Reflect (Cloud mode only), then the section Work in progress

steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory. Memory must be on.
Tap the round button labelled Add memory at the bottom right.
Type a fact in the field What should AGI remember? for example I prefer metric units.
Tap Save.
Check the new card appears in the list with the line Added by you.
Start a new chat and ask a question the fact would answer, then compare with Expected.
S39.10.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the round + button Add memory at the bottom right

S39.11.note: A repeated fact shows an already-known message instead.
steps: Make sure Memory is on (Settings > Assistant > Memory).
Open the chat tab and type Remember that I like short answers.
Send the message.
Look for the status line Saved to memory: followed by the fact.
Open Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the fact is in the list.
S39.11.where: Chat tab: type Remember that ... in the message box and send

S39.12.needs: Memory and the generate switch on; a normal chat
S39.12.note: The client-side capture in the code runs only in Local mode and is off for temporary chats.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Turn on Memory and turn on the switch Generate memory from chat history.
In a normal chat (not temporary) say a lasting fact, for example I work as a nurse in Leeds.
Wait for the reply to finish, then go back to Settings > Assistant > Memory.
Check a new card appears with the line Learned from a chat, or Learned from the chat title.
S39.12.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch labelled Generate memory from chat history

S39.13.note: A card edited within 60 seconds of being added still says Added.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the pencil button labelled Edit memory on a card.
Change the text in the field labelled Memory content.
Tap Update.
Check the card shows the new text and the line Edited, then ask a chat question that uses it.
S39.13.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the pencil button Edit memory on a card

steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Swipe a memory card to the left to show the red trash button labelled Delete memory.
Tap it and read the alert Delete memory?
Tap Delete.
Check the card is gone and the count has gone down by one.
S39.14.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, swipe a card to the left and tap the red trash button

S39.15.note: Reset also deletes chats? No: the alert says your chats are not deleted.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the red row Reset memory.
Read the alert Reset memory? and tap Cancel first; check nothing was removed.
Tap Reset memory again in the alert.
Check the list says No memories yet and the count is zero.
S39.15.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the red row Reset memory

steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the pin button labelled Pin memory on a card.
Check the card shows the badge Pinned.
Tap the chip Pinned to see only pinned memories.
Compare with Expected: pinned memories are kept at the top and win a conflict.
S39.16.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the pin button Pin memory on a card

S39.17.needs: a memory added by hand, an import, and a chat-learned memory
S39.17.note: The chat-learned line uses the chat title when the chat is known.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Add a memory yourself (S39.10) and read the line under it: Added by you.
Import memories (S39.21) and check the line says Imported.
Find a card learned from a chat and check it says Learned from followed by the chat title.
S39.17.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, read the small line under each memory card

S39.18.needs: a memory you can add and edit
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Add a memory (S39.10) and read the time line, which starts with Added.
Wait a minute, then edit the memory (S39.13).
Check the line now starts with Edited and shows a time such as 2m ago.
S39.18.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, read the time line on each memory card

S39.19.needs: Memory on; a Free or paid account is not needed
S39.19.note: The rule runs automatically on the same topic; the code does not show a control for it.
steps: Add a memory such as I live in Paris (S39.10).
In a chat, say a newer fact on the same topic, for example I now live in London.
Open Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the Paris memory is no longer in the main list.
Open Replaced memories and check the Paris memory is listed there.
Start a chat and ask where you live; the answer should use London.
S39.19.where: Effect is seen in Settings > Assistant > Memory > Replaced memories

labels.text: Pinned, added, then newer memories win. The replaced one is kept here.

steps: Create two memories on the same topic (see S39.19).
Open Settings > Assistant > Memory > Replaced memories.
Read the heading When memories disagree and the rule text.
Tap Use the replaced one instead on the entry to settle it.
Check the list now uses the replaced memory and a chat answer follows it.

labels.text: Choose a text or JSON file

S39.21.needs: a text or JSON file, or some pasted lines
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory. Memory must be on.
Tap the upload button Import memories at the top right.
Pick a source under From (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other).
Paste lines into the box or tap Choose a text or JSON file, then tap Preview.
Select the items, tap the import button, and check the message Added N memories.
S39.21.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the upload button labelled Import memories at the top right

labels.text: Chats, memory, settings and model details, exported on this device.

S39.22.needs: some saved memories; a way to open a .json file
S39.22.note: The file is JSON, not plain text. Cloud memory is exported with Export Cloud data in the AGI Cloud account section.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Data Controls.
Under Local data, tap Export Local Data.
Wait for the progress to finish and choose a place in the share sheet.
Open the saved file agi_data_export.json and find the memory_facts list.
Compare the saved memories with the list in Settings > Assistant > Memory.
S39.22.where: Settings > Assistant > Data Controls > Local data > Export Local Data

labels.text: Personal memories. Workspace memories stay in their workspace.

S39.26.needs: an AGI Cloud account in a workspace, with a workspace memory and a personal chat
S39.26.note: In Local mode the scope line reads Stored on this device only.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud with a workspace and switch to Cloud mode.
Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory; the title says Cloud Memory.
Read the scope line under the count: Personal memories. Workspace memories stay in their workspace., or the workspace name line.
Start a personal chat and ask about a workspace memory; it should not appear.
Compare with Expected.
S39.26.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, read the scope line under the count

labels.text: Won't be saved or use memory, and attachments never leave this device.

S39.28.needs: Memory on, with one saved memory
steps: Open the chat tab and tap the eye-off temporary chat control, or turn on the switch Temporary Chat in Settings > Device > General.
Read the explainer text about temporary chats.
Send Remember that I like tea and ask a question about a saved memory.
Go to Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the new fact was not saved.
Start a normal chat and check the temporary chat content is not used as past-chat context.
S39.28.where: Chat tab: the eye-off button for temporary chat; or Settings > Device > General > Temporary Chat

S39.29.needs: Memory on; use a fake test value only, never a real credential; Never remember needs Cloud mode
S39.29.note: The Never remember row appears only in Cloud mode; Local mode has no term list in the code.
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory. Memory must be on for the switch to work.
Read the switch Include sensitive topics in memory and leave it off to stop sensitive topics being learned from chats.
In Cloud mode, tap Never remember, type a term in Term to never remember, and tap Add term.
In the chat tab, send Remember that my password is a fake test value; the reply should say Memory never stores ... so I left that out.
Compare with Expected.
S39.29.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch Include sensitive topics in memory; in Cloud mode also Never remember

S39.30.needs: some chats and some memories; this removes data, so use a test account
S39.30.note: Deleting chats does not change memory and resetting memory does not delete chats.
steps: Note how many memories are in Settings > Assistant > Memory.
Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Data Controls and find Delete all local chats under Local chats.
Read the alert Delete all local chats? (it says memory stays), tap Cancel, then tap the button again and confirm.
Go back to Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the memories are still there.
Tap Reset memory on that screen, confirm, and check the chats in the chat tab are still there.
S39.30.where: Settings > Assistant > Data Controls > Local data > Local chats > Delete all local chats (and separately Settings > Assistant > Memory > Reset memory)
